headline: Nearly half a million Palestinians under lockdown, 200+ families forced out at night, soldiers occupying homes as outposts
dek: AJ's Birzeit correspondent reports Hebron's Farsh al-Hawa area is unrecognisable after extensive Israeli demolitions, with nearly half a million Palestinians now under Israeli lockdown and attack across Hebron. More than 200 families were forced to leave their homes in the dead of night, not…
sources: Al Jazeera liveblog, Nour Odeh reporting from Birzeit, occupied West Bank; Hebron municipality; Palestinian Ministry of Education
fault_line: Security operation or a city-wide lockdown? The army says targeted searches; the report says half a million people locked down, families out at night, homes turned into outposts.

sections.what_happened: AJ's Birzeit correspondent reports Hebron's Farsh al-Hawa area is unrecognisable after extensive Israeli demolitions, with nearly half a million Palestinians now under Israeli lockdown and attack across Hebron. More than 200 families were forced to leave their homes in the dead of night, not knowing when they could return, and Israeli soldiers have moved into some of the vacated homes, turning them into military outposts. The Hebron municipality has set up temporary shelters. The Palestinian Ministry of Education issued a special advisory to Hebron schools to keep children at home for the coming two days. Movement across the West Bank is severely restricted, with hundreds of checkpoints that can open and close without warning; AJ cites an average of 77 hours lost per year per Palestinian at checkpoints inside the West Bank.
sections.what_verified: 1 distinct publisher family: Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA). The operation's scale (40 villages, 400+ searches, 40+ arrests) is already recorded from IDF/AJ/ToI sources; the lockdown scale, home occupations and school advisory are AJ-only in-window.
sections.what_disputed: IDF frames the operation as limited and targeted to the gunmen's area of origin, with civilians allowed to leave through designated checkpoints after screening. Displacement totals conflict across sources (Katz ~2,000 vs local reports ~1,500 vs this report's 200+ families for one area), so no single total is settled. The 'nearly half a million under lockdown' figure is AJ's, not an official count.
sections.why_matters: Half a million people under lockdown, 200 families out in the night, soldiers moving into their homes: Hebron's operation is no longer a search -- it is a siege of a city, three days before Israel votes.
sections.context: Background: SUPPLEMENT from AJ Oct 25 liveblog read (00:20 GMT = 04:20 ) -- UPDATE to Hebron operation: nearly half a million Palestinians under lockdown, 200+ families forced out at night, soldiers occupying homes as outposts, schools told to keep children home two days

totw_analysis: Our read: Half a million people under lockdown, 200 families out in the night, soldiers moving into their homes: Hebron's operation is no longer a search -- it is a siege of a city, three days before Israel votes. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Security operation or a city-wide lockdown? The army says targeted searches; the report says half a million people locked down, families out at night, homes turned into outposts.
